title: Superoxide Dismutase Assay Protocol
author: Peter Havel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ywdfxa6
materials: for a typical standard curve. Table

steps.title: Prepare SOD Standard Wells
steps.instruction: Add the Radical Detector and SOD standards to the designated wells on the plate.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µl of diluted Radical Detector to each standard well.
Add 10 µl of Standard (tubes A-G) to each respective well.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Wells
steps.instruction: Add the Radical Detector and samples to the wells, ensuring the sample volume is always 10 µl.

substeps.instruction: For standard samples: add 200 µl of diluted Radical Detector and 10 µl of sample.
For samples using an inhibitor: add 190 µl of diluted Radical Detector, 10 µl of inhibitor, and 10 µl of sample.
If necessary, dilute samples with Sample Buffer (dilute) or concentrate using an Amicon centrifuge concentrator (10,000 MWCO) to ensure activity falls within the standard curve range.

steps.title: Initiate Reactions
steps.instruction: Start the enzymatic reaction by adding the trigger reagent to all wells.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µl of diluted Xanthine Oxidase to all active wells as quickly as possible, noting the precise start time.
For sample background assays, add 20 µl of Sample Buffer instead of Xanthine Oxidase.

steps.title: Mix and Incubate
steps.instruction: Mix the plate contents and incubate under specified conditions.

substeps.instruction: Carefully shake the 96-well plate for a few seconds to mix.
Cover the plate with a plate cover.
Incubate the plate on a shaker for 20 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Measure Absorbance
steps.instruction: Read the absorbance of the plate at 440-460 nm using a plate reader.

steps.title: Calculate SOD Activity
steps.instruction: Process the absorbance data to determine the SOD activity of the samples.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the average absorbance for each standard and sample; subtract sample background absorbance if applicable.
Determine the linearized rate (LR) by dividing the absorbance of Standard A by itself and by the absorbance of all other standards and samples (e.g., LR for Std B = Abs Std A / Abs Std B).
Plot the LR of the SOD standards as a function of final SOD Activity (U/ml) based on Table 1 to create a standard curve.
Calculate sample SOD activity using the linear regression equation from the standard curve, substituting the LR for each sample.
Note: One unit is defined as the amount of enzyme needed for 50% dismutation of the superoxide radical, standardized using the cytochromic c and xanthine oxidase coupled assay.
